Results.ReviewText:
Well I owned a Weber Silver 'A' and it was working fine. My wife decided I needed a new grill so she purchased a Spirit II E-310. 
I do like the extra burner though.
I did have issues assembling E-310 though. The tapped holes in the cast grill body had a burr on the trailing edge of the tapped hole and since I wasn't at my shop where I have all the tools I need to do repairs and fix manufacturing mistakes, I ran a drill bit through the threaded hole and then used an adjustable wrench on the screwdriver to seat the screw completely. Problem solved, you couldn't see the screw head because it was covered by the burned knob plate. 
The second issue was the cheap aluminum guard over the opening for the drip pan. I needed to modify it by bending and trimming to make it fit correctly. Again I think that may have been a casting issue, whatever it's done.
The last gripe I had was a marketing issue. For the life of me I don't know why they used a sticker on the right hand shelf instead of a piece of cardboard with the marketing information. There's that little curved arrow printed on the corner of the sticker letting you know where to start peeling it off. Yeah right, the sticker started to delaminate and now I have a partial sticker on the shelf that looks like stainless steel but attracts a magnet. I guess I need Goop and/or alcohol to remove what is left of it with out scratching it. We'll see.
As far as the grilling goes it's a Weber do I need to explain? If I need to you wouldn't understand. My Silver A was 22 years old and was working fine and lasted a hour on the side of the road with a free sign on it.
I gave it 5 stars because it's a Weber. If there was two categories one for cooking quality and another for fit and finish quality the cooking would have been 5 stars and fit and finish would get 1 because I was upset that I had to make stuff fit and peel a sticker off.
Results.Title: Weber Spirit II E-310 assembly and cooking review.
